chainlink #56: read-only project-state + consolidated-check engine behind `ligature status`/`ligature check`.

chainlink #77, #103: read-only write-set conformance check -- the descriptor's allowed_roots/protected_roots evaluated against the workspace's actual files, behind `ligature write-set-check` and `status --json`'s write_set state. A protected root is ENFORCED rather than accounted for (#103): a file inside one is a violation unless a declaration vouches for that file, and the two location carve-outs #77 shipped (the `ci/` canonical prefix, and any file under a declared crate's specs/ tree) are replaced by recognizing a pipeline artifact through project_state's own discovery, so the protected surface is judged by the artifact system the pipeline actually runs. #114 adds the sanctioned case: this module is the only consumer of the issue-scoped write grants in ci/results/protected-writes.jsonl, consulted on the protected branch only, and it holds the writer's own refusal -- a ledger inside a declared protected root authorizes nothing (status `ledger-protected`), so a trail cannot vouch for its own presence in the surface it must stay outside of.

chainlink #114: the record half of a sanctioned protected-root write -- `ligature authorize-write --issue N --path P --op K --issuer <name>` appends one issue-scoped capability record to ci/results/protected-writes.jsonl, binding the exact path or a bounded pattern, the operation, the issue, issued_at/expires_at, the one-shot flag, a named issuer and a grant id that is a hash of that binding. Every binding is recomputed on read (expiry relation, id, path classification, and the issuer against the descriptor's write_set.authorized_supervisors whitelist), so a record cannot be edited into a different authorization; a refusal writes nothing.
chainlink #79: mechanical evidence-draft promotion -- re-validates a staged evidence/*.json.draft (G1a/G1b), renames it to its target, and records the move, behind `ligature promote-evidence`.

chainlink #58: safe/idempotent init/upgrade + versioned ownership manifest + three-way managed-file classification behind init/doctor/migrate. `inspect()` takes the global `--descriptor` flag so doctor's descriptor gate follows it rather than the manifest's own `descriptor_path` (chainlink #109).

Chainlink #59: canonical assumption registry loader, G21 reference gate (missing/ambiguous/hash-disagreeing/dangling), phase-B deprecation, phase-C reference migration, and the phase-D version mechanism.
Cwd-independent packaged-resource discovery (#57): returns the source root in a checkout, or extracts the bundled ligature_data package via importlib.resources inside a zipapp.

The executable's own identity (#57): content/build hash over the zipapp bundle, product version, bundled schema set, required Python/platform, and self-verification used by `version --verify`, `doctor`, and gate_integrity. Also surfaces the embedded build's source provenance (`source_commit`/`source_dirty`/`working_tree_diff_hash`), #64.

Release build tool (#57): derives the bundle from this inventory, writes a deterministic attested zipapp plus SHA256SUMS/PROVENANCE/NOTICE/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Records the working tree's source provenance (`source_commit`, `source_dirty`, `working_tree_diff_hash`) honestly rather than assuming a clean tree (#64). Source-only; never itself bundled into the artifact.

The path guard shared by the two path-taking validators (#83): `ensure_manifest_path()` pre-flights a CLI's positional argument and `read_manifest_text()` does the same immediately before the read, so a missing path or a directory raises the user-facing `ManifestInputError` (`error: <kind> not found: <path>`, exit 1) instead of escaping as a raw FileNotFoundError/IsADirectoryError traceback.

chainlink #87: the producer gate-g14's achieved side never had -- assembles a work package's assurance report from why3find proof certificates (`proof.json`) and writes it to the manifest's own report.emit path, every field derived from evidence or the manifest, with only the obligation-to-certificate mapping declared by the caller and that declaration checked (concept anchor, containment, staleness), behind `ligature record-assurance`.

vendored_runtime_assets.reason: Registered in scripts/vendored_resources.py:VENDORED_RESOURCES (the sole authoritative declaration, chainlink #55 round 3) and read via vendored_resource_path() by scripts/select_pilot_cluster.py to validate concept specs during pilot-cluster ranking. The only vendor/ file any scripts/*.py actually needs at runtime -- everything else under vendor/ is copied-not-imported logic or prose reference. #57 replaced vendored_resource_path()'s own Path(__file__)-relative body with scripts/resources.py, which uses importlib.resources from a zipapp, so a distributed binary resolves this asset outside a ligature-workspace checkout. Call sites did not change, only that one function's body.

Its snake_case() is copied verbatim into scripts/validate_boundary_contracts.py and referenced (not imported) elsewhere -- kept as the audit trail proving the copy matches the source, per this project's own concept-to-code boundary rule (never edit the submodule; report modifications in docs/concept-to-code-modifications.md).
